results.outcome: PaO2/FiO2 in ARDS patients with IAH (first physiological outcome reported in abstract results; no primary outcome named by authors)
results.numerical_result: PaO2/FiO2 (mmHg) ARDS+IAH: 209±50 under ARDSnet protocol vs 272±40 under Ptp, P=0.001
results.result_location: Table 3, page 4; also reported in text page 4 ('In ARDS patients with IAH, the PaO2/FiO2, A–aDO2 and SaO2 with PEEP guided by Ptp improved significantly than ARDSnet protocol')

1.1.support: The report states 'A randomized, crossover study was conducted' and Figure 2 shows 'Randomized', but no method of sequence generation is described.

1.2.support: I looked for any description of allocation concealment (central allocation, sealed envelopes, or similar) and found none in the report.

1.3.support: Table 1 compares baseline characteristics of ARDS+IAH versus ARDS patients (the stratification groups), but no baseline data are presented separately for the two randomization sequences, so imbalance at the start of the first period by sequence cannot be judged.

S.1.support: I looked for the numbers of participants allocated to each sequence (Ptp-first vs ARDSnet-first) and found only group sizes by stratum (n=7 IAH, n=8 non-IAH) in Figure 2; sequence sizes are not reported.

S.2.support: The difference of two groups was compared with the use of paired sample student's t test.

S.3.support: Patients were ventilated 30 minutes at each PEEP level with no washout described; after the first period there is only 'Baseline ventilation and measurement' before crossover, and no time is reported for carryover of recruitment/PEEP effects to disappear.

2.1.support: Sedation was given ... to maintain a Ramsay score of 5–6 (no spontaneous breath) throughout the study and paralyzed with vecuronium if necessary.

2.2.support: PEEP levels and the FiO2 of each patient were titrated by Ptp and ARDSnet protocol; ventilator settings were necessarily visible to clinicians delivering ventilation, and no blinding is described.

2.3.support: I looked for deviations from the intended PEEP-titration interventions arising because of the trial context and found no report of such deviations.

2.4.support: Conditional on 2.3 being Y/PY; 2.3 was answered NI.

2.5.support: Conditional on 2.4 being Y/PY; 2.4 was answered NA.

2.6.support: The difference of two groups was compared with the use of paired sample student's t test; a paired analysis including both periods is appropriate for estimating the effect of assignment in this crossover trial.

2.7.support: Conditional on N/PN/NI to 2.6; 2.6 was answered Y.

3.1.support: Of 15 eligible ARDS patients receiving mechanical ventilation, seven ARDS patients with IAH and eight ARDS patients without IAH were included in the study; all 15 appear to contribute to the reported results, and no missing outcome data are described.
3.1.location: page 3, Characteristics of the patients; Figure 1, page 2

3.2.support: Conditional on N/PN/NI to 3.1; 3.1 was answered Y.

3.3.support: Conditional on N/PN to 3.2; 3.2 was answered NA.

3.4.support: Conditional on Y/PY/NI to 3.3; 3.3 was answered NA.

4.1.support: All blood gas measurements were performed using an automated blood gas analyser; PaO2/FiO2 is measured with standard, appropriate methods.
4.1.location: page 2, Haemodynamics and blood gas analysis

4.2.support: Blood gas samples were collected via the same arterial catheter and analysed with the same automated analyser at the same time point (30 minutes after each ventilation phase) in both periods.
4.2.location: page 2, Haemodynamics and blood gas analysis; page 3, Study design

4.3.support: No blinding of clinicians or assessors to the PEEP-titration method is described; the ventilator settings made the assigned intervention evident to care providers.

4.4.support: PaO2/FiO2 was derived from blood gas analysis performed using an automated blood gas analyser, an objective measurement not amenable to influence by knowledge of the assigned intervention.
4.4.location: page 2, Haemodynamics and blood gas analysis

4.5.support: Conditional on Y/PY/NI to 4.4; 4.4 was answered N.

5.1.support: I looked for a pre-specified analysis plan or protocol finalized before unblinded data were available and found none in the report; no trial registration or protocol reference is given.

5.2.support: No primary outcome is named and oxygenation is reported in multiple forms (PaO2/FiO2, A–aDO2, SaO2, PaO2); without a protocol I cannot determine whether the reported PaO2/FiO2 result was selected on the basis of the results.

5.3.support: Only a paired t-test comparison of the two methods is presented for each variable, with no alternative analyses reported, so opportunity for selection among analyses appears limited; no analysis plan is available to confirm.

5.4.support: Data from both periods contribute to the result being assessed; the paired t-test used measurements from both the ARDSnet and Ptp ventilation periods.

D1.rationale: The report gives no information on sequence generation or allocation concealment (1.1 NI, 1.2 NI, 1.3 NI), so the algorithm yields some concerns; there is no evidence the randomization was flawed, but confidence in the randomization process is reduced.

DS.rationale: Sequence sizes were not reported (S.1 NI) and the paired t-test did not account for period effects (S.2 N). More importantly, each period lasted only 30 minutes with no washout before crossover, so carryover of PEEP-induced recruitment and lung-mechanical effects into the second period is plausible (S.3 N). Under the tool's algorithm, N/PN/NI to S.3 leads to a high risk of bias from period and carryover effects. Any carryover would tend to blur the contrast between periods, with a direction that is unpredictable.

D2.rationale: Patients were deeply sedated and paralyzed (2.1 N); clinicians delivering ventilation were necessarily aware of the assigned PEEP strategy (2.2 Y) but no deviations arising from the trial context were reported (2.3 NI), and the paired analysis (2.6 Y) was appropriate for the effect of assignment.

D3.rationale: Outcome data appear available for all 15 randomized patients in both periods; no missing outcome data are reported (3.1 Y).

D4.rationale: PaO2/FiO2 was measured with an automated blood gas analyser using identical methods and timing in both periods (4.1 N, 4.2 N). Although assessors were unblinded (4.3 Y), the outcome is an objective laboratory measurement unlikely to be influenced by knowledge of the intervention (4.4 N).

D5.rationale: No protocol or pre-specified analysis plan is available (5.1 NI) and, with no primary outcome declared, the possibility that the PaO2/FiO2 result in the IAH stratum was selected from multiple oxygenation measurements on the basis of the results cannot be excluded (5.2 NI, 5.3 PN).

overall.rationale: The study is judged at high risk of bias in the period and carryover domain (DS) because of the very short 30-minute periods with no washout and an analysis that ignores period effects; there are additional some concerns in the randomization and selective reporting domains.
